answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because raven only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, willow is enforced in the ledger: The network tolerates clones that do real work; it only refuses ones that add no signal. Any voyage approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
